newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian judge expected to rule in B Band case.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian judge expected to rule in B Band case.

text.p: A Brazilian judge is mulling a request for an injunction that could suspend the government's plan to offer B Band cellular telephone concessions and he may announce his ruling later Monday, a court official said.
However, the proceedings have been held up because the court was undergoing refurbishment and there was a chance the announcement might be delayed, the official said.
A telecommunications workers' trade union has alleged that the government's plan to tender out B Band concessions is unconstitutional.
The government intends to lodge an appeal should the judge rule in favor of the injunction request, a Communications Ministry spokesman said.

The case is separate to a challenge to the B Band program in the Supreme Court brought by left-wing opposition parties. The tribunal decided Thursday to put that case on hold for 10 days to request further information on the program.

The government has invited private groups to bid by April 7 for tenders for 10 concessions to run regional cellphone services over 15 years, the first stage of Brazil's telecommunications privatization.
